sources.title: S. M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1 (December 1997), 238 PDF pages
sources.locator: Ch. 1 'Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime' printed pp. 25-27 (PDF pp. 32-34): worldlines, proper time and four-velocity. Ch. 2 'Manifolds' printed pp. 50-51 (PDF pp. 57-58): Riemann normal coordinates. Ch. 3 'Curvature' printed pp. 57-61 (PDF pp. 64-68): the covariant derivative and the connection coefficients. Printed pp. 64-65 (PDF pp. 71-72): parallel transport. Printed pp. 68-71 (PDF pp. 75-78): geodesics and the affine parameter. Printed pp. 72-73 (PDF pp. 79-80): the exponential map. Ch. 4 'Gravitation' printed pp. 97-106 (PDF pp. 104-113): the principle of equivalence and physics in curved spacetime.

contents.name: Ch. 1 'worldlines', 'proper time' (1.97) and 'four-velocity' (1.98)-(1.99): the timelike worldline, the proper-time integral and the unit-normalized four-velocity (printed pp. 25-27, PDF pp. 32-34)
contents.support: The lecture notes' worldline, proper time and four-velocity conventions, including U^mu = dx^mu/dtau and its normalization, are the source restated by the definition of timelike worldlines, proper time and four-velocity.

contents.name: Ch. 2 'Riemann normal coordinates': g_{mu nu}(p) = eta_{mu nu} and the first-order normal form at a point, with the local-Lorentz-frame reading (printed pp. 50-51, PDF pp. 57-58)
contents.support: Riemann normal coordinates with the metric in first-order normal form at p are the lecture-notes version of the point-normal and exponential chart theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'the covariant derivative': the connection (3.1)-(3.4), the Christoffel symbols (3.21)-(3.27), metric compatibility (3.30) and the uniqueness of the Christoffel connection (printed pp. 57-61, PDF pp. 64-68)
contents.support: The Christoffel formula, metric compatibility and the statement that the two conditions single out one connection are the lecture-notes route used by the existence-and-uniqueness theorem.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'parallel transport': the equation of parallel transport (3.31), the definition along a path and the preservation of inner products by a metric-compatible connection (printed pp. 64-65, PDF pp. 71-72)
contents.support: The parallel transport equation, its first-order ODE character and inner-product preservation are the lecture-notes source of the parallel-transport lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 3 proper-time functional and fixed-endpoint first variation (3.48)-(3.56), printed pp. 69-70 (PDF pp. 76-77)
contents.support: The variational derivation of the geodesic equation from the proper-time integral is the lecture-notes route paralleled by the first-variation lemma.

contents.name: Ch. 3 'the exponential map' (3.60)-(3.62): exp_p(v) = gamma_{p,v}(1), invertibility near zero and radial coordinates (printed pp. 72-73, PDF pp. 79-80)
contents.support: The source defines exp_p by affine geodesic evaluation at time 1 and describes its local inverse/radial coordinates. The item proves its maximal-domain, scaling, smoothness and inverse assertions locally from exact ODE suppliers; no global source-domain claim is adopted.

contents.name: Ch. 3 from 'curvature' proper onward: the Riemann tensor, its symmetries, geodesic deviation and the Einstein equation sections (printed pp. 74-96, PDF pp. 81-103)
contents.reason: The Riemann tensor, geodesic deviation and curvature identities belong to the curvature-and-tides page, which owns the second derivatives of the metric that this page deliberately does not claim.

contents.name: Ch. 4 'the principle of equivalence' and 'physics in curved spacetime': the equivalence-principle motivation and the transcription of physical laws to curved spacetime (printed pp. 97-106, PDF pp. 104-113)
contents.support: The equivalence-principle discussion is cited as motivation for the adopted clock and free-fall rules; the postulate itself is adopted, not derived from the discussion.

contents.name: Ch. 4 'the Newtonian limit' and the remainder of the gravitation chapter (printed pp. 106-113, PDF pp. 113-120)
contents.reason: The weak-field and Newtonian-limit sections are the flat-and-Newtonian-bridges page's content; this page uses no weak-field approximation.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity (Cambridge, October 12, 2022 revision), 126 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 3.1-3.2 'The Levi-Civita connection' printed pp. 33-37 (PDF pp. 34-38): connection coefficients (3.23), the Koszul-type derivation (3.24)-(3.29), the uniqueness theorem, the Christoffel formula (3.33) and the remark on general connections. Section 3.3 'Geodesics' printed pp. 37-38 (PDF pp. 38-39): the geodesic equation, affine parameters, the exercise on constant g(X,X), the free-particle geodesic postulate, the clock remark and the uniqueness of the affinely parametrized geodesic through (p, X_p). Section 3.4 'Normal coordinates' printed pp. 38-40 (PDF pp. 39-41): the geodesic flow, normal coordinates and the lemmas Gamma^mu_{(nu rho)}(p) = 0 and g_{mu nu, rho}(p) = 0. Section 6.4 'Postulates of General Relativity' printed pp. 57-58 (PDF pp. 58-59): the equivalence principle, the geodesic postulate and the test-body idealization.

contents.name: Sections 3.1-3.2: the Levi-Civita connection, the Koszul derivation (3.23)-(3.29), the uniqueness theorem, the Christoffel formula (3.33) and metric compatibility (printed pp. 33-37, PDF pp. 34-38)
contents.support: The Koszul form, the proof that its connection is torsion-free and metric compatible, and the uniqueness statement are the lecture-notes route restated and proved by the existence-and-uniqueness theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.2 remark: any connection can be written as the Levi-Civita connection plus a (1,2) tensor field (printed p. 36, PDF p. 37)
contents.support: The remark that connections form an affine space over (1,2) tensors is the lecture-notes setting of the counterexample's non-metric-compatible deformation of the flat connection.

contents.name: Section 3.3: the geodesic equation nabla_X X = 0, the affine parameter and its two-parameter freedom, the non-affine equation nabla_Y Y = f Y, the exercise that g(X,X) is constant along a geodesic, the postulate that free particles move on geodesics, and the remark that clocks measuring proper time differ only by their zero (printed pp. 37-38, PDF pp. 38-39)
contents.support: The free-particle geodesic postulate and the proper-time/clock remark are the lecture-notes source of the adopted clock and free-fall clauses of the postulate.

contents.name: Section 3.3: existence and uniqueness of the affinely parametrized geodesic through (p, X_p) and constancy of the causal character of a geodesic (printed pp. 38-39, PDF pp. 39-40)
contents.support: The existence-and-uniqueness statement for geodesics with prescribed initial data is the lecture-notes version of the initial-value part of the exponential-map theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.3 remark and worked formula: reparametrized geodesics satisfy nabla_Y Y = f Y and a geodesic is not affinely parametrized in a general parameter (printed p. 38, PDF p. 39)
contents.support: The equation nabla_Y Y = f Y for a non-affine parameter is the general statement that the worked example verifies on beta(s) = (s^2, 0, 0, 0).

contents.name: Section 3.4: normal coordinates at p, the lemma Gamma^mu_{(nu rho)}(p) = 0, the lemma g_{mu nu, rho}(p) = 0 and the derivation from straight geodesics through p (printed pp. 38-40, PDF pp. 39-41)
contents.support: The construction of normal coordinates and the vanishing of the connection components and first metric derivatives at p are the lecture-notes version of the point-normal chart theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.4 closing discussion: normal coordinates are a pointwise first-order statement and derivatives of the metric away from p need not vanish (printed pp. 39-40, PDF pp. 40-41)
contents.support: The pointwise-only nature of the normal-form identities is the lecture-notes statement that the scope remark records against second-order or neighborhood-flatness readings.

contents.name: Section 6.4 'Postulates of General Relativity': the equivalence-principle formulation, the geodesic postulate for test bodies (timelike and null) and the test-body idealization (printed pp. 57-58, PDF pp. 58-59)
contents.support: The geodesic postulate and test-body idealization are the second independent treatment behind the adopted free-fall clause and its exclusions.

contents.name: Section 3.4 and chapter 4 exercises and sections on curvature, geodesic deviation and the Riemann tensor (printed pp. 40-56, PDF pp. 41-57)
contents.reason: Curvature, the Riemann tensor and geodesic deviation belong to the curvature-and-tides page; this page's normal-coordinate theorem is explicitly silent at second order.

contents.name: Section 6.4 postulates on the field equation and on matter: spacetime is a 4d Lorentzian manifold with the Einstein equation and stress-energy of matter (printed pp. 57-58, PDF pp. 58-59)
contents.reason: The field equation and the stress-energy postulates are the Einstein-and-matter page's content; the free-fall page adopts no field equation and no matter model.

sources.title: D. Tong, General Relativity (Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019), 290 PDF pages
sources.locator: Sections 1.1.1-1.1.2 printed pp. 24-30 (PDF pp. 31-37): the point-particle action, the geodesic equation (1.28)-(1.30), the affine parameter discussion, mass independence and null geodesics for light. Sections 3.1.3 The metric isomorphism, the inverse metric and the volume form. Section 3.2.3 'The Levi-Civita Connection' printed pp. 109-111 (PDF pp. 116-118): the compatibility conditions (3.16)-(3.17) and the Christoffel symbols. Section 3.3.1 'Geodesics Revisited' printed pp. 119-121 (PDF pp. 126-128). Section 3.3.2 'Normal Coordinates' printed pp. 121-122 (PDF pp. 128-129): g_{mu nu}(p) = eta_{mu nu}, vanishing first derivatives and the counting argument for the second derivatives, and 'The Equivalence Principle' printed pp. 122-123 (PDF pp. 129-130).

contents.name: Sections 1.1.1-1.1.2: the point-particle action, its Euler-Lagrange equation (1.28)-(1.30), the affine parameter, the remark that the geodesic equation does not depend on the mass, and null geodesics for light (printed pp. 24-30, PDF pp. 31-37)
contents.support: The action derivation of the geodesic equation, the mass-independence remark and the null case for light are the third treatment behind the adopted free-fall and light-ray clauses.

contents.name: Section 1.1.2: proper time as the affine parameter of a timelike worldline and the four-velocity normalization (printed pp. 27-29, PDF pp. 34-36)
contents.support: The statement that proper time is an affine parameter and that the tangent is unit-normalized is the lecture-notes counterpart of the proper-time parametrization in the lemma.

contents.name: Section 3.2.3 'The Levi-Civita Connection': the compatibility conditions (3.16)-(3.17), the Christoffel symbols (3.16)-(3.17) and the uniqueness of the compatible torsion-free connection (printed pp. 109-111, PDF pp. 116-118)
contents.support: The Levi-Civita connection defined by metric compatibility and torsion freedom is the lecture-notes statement whose defining identities the conformal-metric example verifies directly.

contents.name: Section 3.3.1 'Geodesics Revisited': a geodesic is a curve tangent to X with nabla_X X = 0, affine parametrization, and the consequence of nabla_X g = 0 that a parallelly transported vector keeps its angle with the geodesic (printed pp. 119-121, PDF pp. 126-128)
contents.support: The constancy of inner products along parallel transport and the affine-parameter characterization are the lecture-notes version of the parallel-transport-and-speed lemma.

contents.name: Section 3.3.2 'Normal Coordinates': geodesics through p as straight coordinate lines, g_{mu nu}(p) = eta_{mu nu}, vanishing first derivatives, and the counting argument that the second derivatives cannot generally be made to vanish (printed pp. 121-122, PDF pp. 128-129)
contents.support: The counting argument and the explicit statement that normal coordinates cannot generally kill the second metric derivatives back the counterexample refuting the second-order claim.

contents.name: Section 3.3.2 'Normal Coordinates': the exponential-map construction of the coordinates, the geodesic straight-line form x^mu(tau) = tau X^mu and the first-order metric form (printed pp. 120-122, PDF pp. 127-129)
contents.support: The exponential-map construction of normal coordinates and the straight-line form of geodesics through p are the lecture-notes version of the exponential chart theorem.

contents.name: Section 3.3.2 'The Equivalence Principle': the locally flat metric reading of normal coordinates, and its limitations (printed pp. 122-123, PDF pp. 129-130)
contents.support: The local-inertial-frame reading and its stated limitations are the lecture-notes material that the scope remark separates from the first-order mathematics.

contents.name: Sections 3.4 onwards: curvature, the Riemann tensor, the Einstein equation and the Schwarzschild solution (printed pp. 125-260, PDF pp. 132-267)
contents.reason: Curvature, the field equation and the vacuum solution belong to the curvature-and-tides, Einstein-and-matter and spherical-vacuum pages, none of which this page consumes.
